text: We will not interfere with domestic politics in Myanmar, but the solution must ultimately involve national reconciliation amongst all the domestic stakeholders living there.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked about the continued relevance of multilateralism.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As a small state, the observance of international law is vital for our sovereignty and independence.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But the fact remains, we live in an increasingly fragmented world, with the erosion of shared rules for the global commons and where more frequent resort to unilateral action.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is, therefore, even more important for Singapore to strongly advocate adherence to international law and to actively contribute to shaping global norms.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mr Alex Yam asked about the implications of the war in Ukraine.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There are many other global challenges such as food security, emerging diseases and threats in the cyberspace that require collective action.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The most salient and urgent is climate change, and Singapore is particularly sensitive to this as an alternative energy-disadvantaged and low-lying island state.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore must continue advocating for multilateralism and globalisation, and support for the UN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We do our part to contribute to the multilateral governance of the global commons.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are helping to develop fair, inclusive and well-functioning global carbon markets.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also have a significant role in developing international oceans law, as well as new global norms in cyberspace and in outer space.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ambassador Rena Lee serves as President of the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Intergovernmental Conference, which aims to enhance the sustainable use of our maritime global commons.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore, represented by our Permanent Representative to the UN, Mr Burhan Gafoor, chairs the UN Open-ended Working Group on security of and in the use of information and communications technologies, to build a safe and secure cyberspace for all.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singaporeans are also taking the lead in other international organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For example, Mr Daren Tang serves as Director General of the World Intellectual Property Organization – this is the first time a Singaporean has led a UN agency, while Raja Kumar serves as the President of the Financial Action Task Force – he also happens to be the first Singaporean to have assumed this role.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Strategic and geopolitical tensions are also undermining the multilateral trading system.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore depends on a stable, functioning and free international trading system to make a living, centred around a common set of rules for all.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Remember, our trade volume is three times our GDP.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, we do need to continue to uphold such a system as embodied and represented by the WTO.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also diversify our trade relationships through regional arrangements such as the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) – that is ASEAN-10, plus China, Australia, New Zealand, ROK and Japan.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also substantially completed the negotiations for the Mercosur-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (FTA), and we have also signed on to the Pacific Alliance-Singapore FTA.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Mind you, all these have been signed during the last couple of years when there was a pushback against globalisation, against free trade and in fact, the world being disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we have been able to double down on the cause of free trade.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will need to continue to seize opportunities in global integration and also seize opportunities in emerging areas like the digital economy and sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have concluded Digital Economy Agreements (DEAs) with several like-minded partners.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are entering a period of intense superpower rivalry, global economic disruption and looming climate change, and all these within a more fragmented, turbulent world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is worth recalling the words of Mr Lee Kuan Yew: "We have to live with the world as it is, not as we wish it should be." Singapore and Singaporeans must approach all these challenges with a combination of realism and quiet confidence.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Do not underestimate the external dangers, but neither be overwhelmed by them.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are one of the few countries whose unity has, in fact, strengthened after the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That is why there is strong interest from businesses, investors and entrepreneurs from elsewhere, queueing up to come to Singapore and to plug into our ecosystem.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They recognise and appreciate the stability and consistency with which we have run our affairs, both internally and externally.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This reputation for consistency and stability, and high levels of public trust and unity provides us with the strength and the resilience to manage our foreign policy challenges in a very hazardous world.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Second Minister for Foreign Affairs Dr Mohamad Maliki Osman.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, Mr Don Wee, Dr Wan Rizal and Ms Sylvia Lim asked about our relations with Malaysia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Malaysia and Singapore are deeply intertwined, with strong people-to-people, cultural and economic linkages.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There is a high tempo of two-way exchanges and visits.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also devote considerable resources to deepening our links with the various Malaysian states.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ultimately, the relationship between Singapore and Malaysia is undergirded by enduring people-to-people linkages, which we are committed to strengthening into the next generation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to speak briefly in Malay.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   As a small nation without natural resources, our foreign policy is to strengthen our relations with as many nations and to stay relevant in a rapidly changing world.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the same time, we have to be united and concur that our foreign policy begins at home.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Every citizen plays a role towards advancing Singapore's interests in the international arena.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore's foreign policy will always be based on our principles and interests.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Every choice and decision we make prioritises Singapore’s interests.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are confronting a period of intense superpower competition and a more fragmented and turbulent world.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But Singapore approaches these challenges from a position of strength.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our political and economic stability, as well as our consistency in managing our affairs, are valued by others around the world.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the same time, our unity and public trust are crucial to navigating foreign policy challenges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In this regard, Singaporeans trust their Government and remain more united than ever before.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I urge Singaporeans to be more aware of our external environment, so that they know the realities of the world we live in, but also have the hope and confidence that, if we stay united, we can emerge from these challenges stronger.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Therefore, we should continue to endeavour to strengthen relations with our neighbours, especially our most immediate neighbours.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said during Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's visit to Singapore in January, Singapore and Malaysia share a relationship quite unlike any other.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A key pillar in our relations is the deep familial ties, as well as our shared history, languages and cultures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singaporeans and Malaysians frequently visit each other’s countries, whether for work, play or visiting relatives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, we cannot take the current strength of our people-to-people relationship for granted.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must ensure our younger generation are invested in it.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must create opportunities for young Singaporeans and Malaysians to engage one another, and spend time together to learn about and appreciate one another’s perspectives and aspirations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our education system plays an important role in this, especially now with the easing of COVID-19-related travel restrictions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As we know, we need to enhance in-person interactions to form close-knit friendships.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Similarly, for classroom concepts, such as shared cultures and civilisations, to come to life – we need in-person interactions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: So, I was delighted that 41 junior college students in the Malay Language Elective Programme had the chance to visit Selangor and Ipoh last year to attend classes at the Universiti Putra Malaysia where they learned about Malay heritage and even tried their hand at making fermented fish in Kampung Beng in Ipoh!

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Importantly, such educational exchanges are not limited to our students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Beyond education, we are also enhancing cultural and religious exchanges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: On the cultural front, with the Government's support, practitioners of various Malay art forms in Singapore are engaging more widely with Malaysian artists and audiences.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As close neighbours, however, we acknowledge that there will be differences on some issues from time to time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But we must seek practical ways in managing these bilateral issues and always prioritise working together to improve our peoples' lives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We intend to continue this spirit of pragmatic cooperation with Prime Minister Anwar and his team, as we build a Singapore-Malaysia relationship which our future younger generations can be proud of.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, allow me to continue my speech in English.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked about how we are stepping up our cooperation with Indonesia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As the largest economy in ASEAN and an immediate neighbour, Indonesia is a natural investment destination.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last year, I visited six Indonesian provinces for bilateral and G20 meetings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I met a wide range of political and business leaders, as well as Singaporeans living in Indonesia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Among these regions, the Riau islands (KEPRI) is geographically the closest to Singapore and we have worked well with leaders through the pandemic and we will continue to support each other's recovery.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There are new growth areas, for example, Indonesian companies are keen to boost exports to Singapore in the agri-food and energy sectors, which aligns with Singapore's efforts to strengthen domestic food supply and security.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Economic Development Board, together with Enterprise Singapore and Singapore Food Agency, have been working to increase our imports of hydroponic vegetables from Batam.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The MFA also supports these efforts by offering relevant capacity-building courses under the Singapore Cooperation Programme (SCP) for Indonesian government officials.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Indonesia is an important partner in maintaining the continued prosperity and security in the region, strengthening ASEAN centrality and relevance, and upholding the multilateral rules-based order.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In November 2022, the Prime Minister attended the successful G20 Summit hosted by Indonesia against the backdrop of heightened global tensions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore was happy to support Indonesia's G20 Presidency as it is important to strengthen multilateral platforms.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore is also extending our full support to Indonesia as ASEAN Chair this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore will host the next Singapore-Indonesia Leaders' Retreat.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will be a good opportunity for our leaders to enhance the bilateral relationship and explore new areas of opportunities and cooperation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have a special, unique and close relationship with Brunei.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As mentioned by Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong visited Brunei at the start of the year, reaffirmed Singapore's long-term commitment to nurturing this special relationship into the next generation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition, Prime Minister Lee and Mdm Ho Ching attended His Majesty's 76th birthday celebration in July 2022.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We were honoured to welcome His Majesty Sultan Bolkiah last year on his fifth state visit to Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: That same month, His Royal Highness Crown Prince Billah visited Singapore for the eighth Singapore-Brunei Young Leaders' Programme, when both sides agreed to establish a bilateral scholarship programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain asked about how we have built on our relations with Brunei following the visits last year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With Cambodia and Thailand, Singapore has worked closely with both to support of their successful chairmanships of ASEAN and APEC in 2022 respectively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also expanding our collaboration in emerging areas, such as the digital economy, innovation and sustainability.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We celebrated the 50th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations with Vietnam and the 10th anniversary of our Strategic Partnership.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Vietnamese Prime Minister Pham Minh Chinh visited Singapore earlier this month.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We look forward to a series of high-level exchanges to strengthen our trade and investment links, and expand cooperation in new areas, like renewable energy, carbon credits, digital economy and sustainable infrastructure.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr of the Philippines visited Singapore last year for his first overseas trip since taking office.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have expanded our partnership with the Philippines, in areas ranging from digital cooperation, data privacy and counterterrorism, to water collaboration, urban development and the deployment of healthcare workers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last June, we started importing hydropower from Laos under the Lao PDR-Thailand-Malaysia-Singapore Power Integration Project (LTMS-PIP).

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This marks the first renewable energy import into Singapore and serves as a pathfinder towards an eventual ASEAN Power Grid.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition to the warm relations with our neighbours, ASEAN remains a cornerstone of Singapore's foreign policy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As noted by Mr Henry Kwek, the combined GDP of all 10 ASEAN countries currently stands at about US$3 trillion.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN is expected to become the fourth largest single market in the world by 2030.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN is home to over 660 million people, with 60% of our population under the age of 35 – a significant demographic dividend.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We intend to enhance regional economic integration through ASEAN-led frameworks and the FTAs, which provide greater economic opportunities for our Member States.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ASEAN is also pursuing FTAs with new partners like Canada.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition, we are upgrading existing ones, such as our ASEAN-China Free Trade Area and ASEAN's FTA with Australia and New Zealand to ensure that these arrangements remain relevant in the post-pandemic economy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Beyond trade, ASEAN is looking at how to best harness digital technology to transform our economies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, the ASCN Online Portal, that seeks to provide up-to-date information on ASEAN smart cities priorities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It can help position Singapore as a marketplace for ASEAN's smart cities solutions and support Singapore firms exploring commercially viable smart city projects in the region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, the ASEAN Smart City Investment Toolkit provides information for various options available for funding and financing smart city initiatives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Such initiatives provide opportunities for our people and businesses to tap into the digital economy and narrow the digital divide within our societies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As noted by Mr Seah Kian Peng, it has been two years since the coup in Myanmar and the region remains grave.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore and ASEAN remain deeply disappointed with the lack of progress in the implementation of the ASEAN Five-Point Consensus.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue engaging them at the civil service level.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Miss Rachel Ong and Mr Louis Ng asked about the humanitarian assistance that ASEAN and Singapore have provided to Myanmar.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The dire situation in Myanmar has, unfortunately, diminished the prospect of a safe, voluntary and dignified return of refugees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition, Singapore has contributed US$100,000 to the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on disaster management.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will work with relevant partners to scope our assistance in a way that would meet the specific needs and circumstances in the affected countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Looking beyond our immediate region, we are working to further deepen collaboration with other key partners.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked about Singapore's relations with India post-pandemic, the steps taken both to deepen bilateral cooperation, as well as ensure that India remains engaged in the region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: India is an important friend and partner to Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last September, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, Minister Gan Kim Yong and Minister S Iswaran were in New Delhi to participate in the inaugural India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable with their Indian counterparts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This leaders-driven platform allows both sides to explore potential collaboration in emerging areas, such as food security, energy and green projects, and digitalisation, including enhancing digital connectivity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singaporeans will now be able to send and receive funds from their family and friends in India in a safe, simple and cost-effective manner.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We commemorated the 30th Anniversary of ASEAN-India Dialogue Relations and the establishment of the ASEAN-India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP) in 2022.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The CSP will serve as a springboard for mutually beneficial cooperation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will create more opportunities for our people, and enhance contributions to an open and inclusive region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: India assumed the G20 Presidency in 2023 and we thank India for inviting Singapore to participate in G20 meetings this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore will continue to contribute constructively in the G20 framework, including in our capacity as Convenor of the Global Governance Group (3G), with a view to enhance the inclusiveness of the G20 process and strengthen the global governance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked how we can enhance our relations with Australia and New Zealand.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With Australia, we are constantly exploring ambitious areas of cooperation under our CSP.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Singapore-Australia Green Economy Agreement (GEA) that Minister Vivian mentioned earlier is one such example.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The GEA will reduce barriers to cross-border trade in clean energy, as well as green trade and investment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This, in turn, promotes the growth of green sector in our economy and creates new job opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We established a new "Climate Change and Green Energy" Pillar under the Singapore-New Zealand Enhanced Partnership in April 2022.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This will pave the way for low-carbon and sustainability solutions, and include initiatives on energy transition technology, carbon markets, sustainable transport and waste management.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Meanwhile, we will continue to strengthen our engagement in the Middle East and Central Asia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain asked about our relations with the Middle East, and Singapore's role in the Israeli-Palestine conflict.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our ties with the key Gulf countries remains excellent, and there is growing interest to deepen cooperation in areas like renewable energy, which the Gulf states have ambitious plans on.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We look forward to elevating our ties with Saudi Arabia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We enjoy excellent ties with the United Arab Emirates (UAE), our top trading partner in the Middle East.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As small states and hubs in our respective regions, we share many mutual interests.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There has been healthy exchange of visits between the UAE and Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In May 2022, I accompanied the President to attend the mourning for the late UAE President Sheikh Khalifa.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Abu Dhabi-Singapore Joint Forum was held earlier this month and I will co-chair the Singapore-UAE Joint Committee meeting later this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Several high-level exchanges also took place last year with other Gulf countries.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Minister K Shanmugam and I had good discussions with our counterparts during the inaugural Singapore-Oman Strategic Dialogue in December 2022.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I plan to visit Oman later this year to take a look at some of those opportunities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With Qatar, our third-largest trading partner in the region, we look forward to continued engagement as fellow small states.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Last year, Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean, Minister Shanmugam and I made separate visits to meet various Qatari leaders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Later this year, Singapore will host the eighth High Level Joint Committee to explore new areas of cooperation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We remain committed and concerned by the escalation of the violence in Israel and the West Bank.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Certainly, we are always very concerned to the escalation of violence there.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are saddened by the loss of lives on both sides.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There can be no justification for attacks on innocent civilians.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Both Israelis and Palestinians deserve to live in peace and security.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As a friend of both sides, we continue to urge both Israel and the Palestinian Authority to return to direct negotiations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: A two-state solution requires both sides to have the political will to negotiate with each other in good faith and make the necessary concessions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Such unilateral moves will only further heighten tensions and undermine any prospect for peace.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We urge all parties to avoid taking further unilateral actions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The status quo at the Temple Mount/Haram Al Sharif should be maintained.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition, Singapore supports Jordan's custodianship of the Christian and Muslim holy sites in Jerusalem.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our ties with the Palestinian Authority remain strong.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Both Minister Vivian and I made separate visits to Ramallah in the West Bank last year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During my visit, I officiated the opening of the Singapore Representative Office there.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In October 2022, we welcomed the visit of Palestinian Authority Prime Minister Dr Mohammad Shtayyeh to Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Prime Minister Shtayyeh was the first high-level Palestinian leader to visit Singapore and he expressed appreciation for Singapore's support for the Palestinian Authority's capacity building efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore will continue to do so through the Enhanced Technical Assistance Package which we had established since 2013.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, given the turbulence and challenges that the world continues to face, it is more important than ever for Singapore to further strengthen our ties with our international partners and friends.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will seek a common cause, including on pressing global issues, as well as in bilateral collaboration.

speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In doing so, we will also find opportunities for the benefit of Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In Mandarin):   Dr Lim Wee Kiak, Ms Janet Ang and Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about the outlook for Singapore-China relations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have kept up our uniquely defined "All-Round Cooperative Partnership Progressing with the Times".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our deepening cooperation in the digital and green economies, as well as on e-commerce, will increase digital connectivity between our countries, foster further business cooperation and better position us for a more sustainable future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is with this forward-looking spirit that our bilateral relations continue to grow from strength to strength, and bring benefits to our peoples and enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the past year, President Halimah and Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong, respectively, had good in-person meetings with President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Keqiang.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last week, I joined Minister Vivian on his visit to China.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also welcomed several delegations from China, most notably, Vice Premier Han Zheng for the 18th JCBC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Such engagements allow us to reconnect in-person with our Chinese friends, which is necessary to build and strengthen trust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We look forward to catching up with old friends, building ties with the new Chinese leadership and further strengthening bilateral relations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, please allow me to continue in English.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Janet Ang asked what could be done to strengthen bilateral engagements with the US.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Prime Minister visited the US twice last year – in March for a bilateral visit and in May for the ASEAN-US Special Summit hosted by President Joe Biden.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Several Cabinet colleagues have also made visits to the US.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In Singapore, we hosted visits by key members of the Biden Administration last year, including four Cabinet members Secretary of Defence Lloyd Austin, Secretary of Energy Jennifer Granholm, Secretary of Homeland Security Alejandro Mayorkas and US Trade Representative Katherine Tai.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also hosted visits by Members of Congress, including one led by then-US Speaker Nancy Pelosi.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The intensity of engagements reflects the breadth and depth of our bilateral relationship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Greater engagement with the US will benefit not just Singapore but also our region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: That is why Singapore participates actively in the US' Indo-Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Singapore is working closely with the US and other IPEF members to develop an open, inclusive and flexible framework that brings tangible benefits for our workers, businesses and communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The US is the chair of APEC this year and has chosen the theme of "Creating a Resilient and Sustainable Future for All", to build a more interconnected, innovative and inclusive APEC region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Beyond China and the US, Singapore is also deepening our collaboration with many other like-minded partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Ms Joan Pereira asked about our plans to strengthen cooperation with other countries and partners such as Japan, the ROK, the UK, the EU and Latin America, and with emerging markets, such as those in South Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa and the Pacific Islands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: High-level exchanges were frequent with Japan and the ROK in 2022.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: President Halimah attended the inauguration ceremony of ROK President Yoon Suk-yeol, while Prime Minister made two working visits to Japan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also welcomed Japanese Prime Minister Kishida Fumio's first Official Visit to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Digitalisation is a recurrent theme in our cooperation with Japan and the ROK.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Korea-Singapore Digital Partnership Agreement (DPA) entered into force this January.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to deepen bilateral cooperation with both Japan and the ROK.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Relations with the UK and EU are underpinned by strong economic ties and our common commitment to supporting free trade and a rules-based international order.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have FTAs with both the UK and the EU.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are enhancing connectivity in the digital realm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, our DEA with the UK entered into force last year and we signed a DPA with the EU earlier this month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As the gateway to the region, Singapore can play an active role to promote greater collaboration between Europe and Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We welcome Europe's interest to engage our region through initiatives, such as its €10 billion package for ASEAN under the EU's Global Gateway Initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With Latin America, we have concluded negotiations for an FTA with MERCOSUR and signed an FTA with the Pacific Alliance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Both FTAs represent significant new opportunities for us to engage the fifth and eighth largest economic markets in the world respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are also pursuing other forward-looking initiatives with partners in Latin America, such as on the digital economy, food security and carbon credits collaboration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The latter will help us meet our Nationally Determined Contributions, while bringing sustainable development benefits and facilitating technology collaboration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While some parts of South Asia experienced setbacks last year, long-term growth prospects for the region are positive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In 2022, we welcomed official visits from the Foreign Ministers of Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Pakistan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to build on the warm ties to deepen our collaboration in areas – such as food security, infrastructure development, the digital economy and connectivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have seen an uptick in our engagement with Sub-Saharan Africa.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Prime Minister made his first official visit to Rwanda last June in conjunction with the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Africa has emerged as an engine of growth, and we will do more to engage the continent with 1.4 billion people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, Singapore will deepen our engagement of the South Pacific, and we look forward to attending the Pacific Islands Forum later this year as a newly-admitted Dialogue Partner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As a small country with limited manpower, we only have resident missions in 33 countries and regions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Consequently, we depend on the excellent support of our NRAs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas sought an assessment of the NRA scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our NRAs are reputable individuals both in the public and private sectors, who have distinguished themselves in the fields of their respective professions and have contributed extensively to the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We assess their performance regularly as part of the NRA appointment process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We constantly evaluate our diplomatic relations, review our scope of coverage, and will appoint NRAs to countries of interest to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Besides our contributions to international norm-setting which Minister Vivian had spoken about earlier, Singapore also extends our support to other countries in different ways.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about our contributions to the UNHCR and Miss Cheryl Chan asked how the SCP is evolving to better meet regional and global challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Besides the UNHCR, Singapore makes annual voluntary financial contributions to a range of UN funds and programmes, and other international organisations and humanitarian mandates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some examples are the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), UN Development Programme, the International Committee for the Red Cross, UN Women and United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We review the quantum of our contributions regularly and have increased our contribution to OCHA this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Singapore focuses especially on capacity-building in developing countries by extending technical assistance and training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Twenty twenty-two marked the 30th anniversary of the SCP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We refined our health-related courses to strengthen pandemic resilience and gave greater focus to digital transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also launched a new Sustainability Action Package to support the capacity-building priorities of developing countries on sustainability and climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Cheng Hsing Yao asked about MFA's consular assistance to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Singaporeans travel very widely and sometimes need help urgently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: During the pandemic, we resolved to "leave no Singaporean behind".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Consular work is, thus, one of MFA's core functions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MFA officers in our Overseas Missions have worked tirelessly under challenging conditions to respond swiftly to changing local environments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, our Consulate-General in Shanghai partnered with the Singapore Global Network and the Singaporean community groups to distribute basic necessities to Singaporeans who faced difficulties in procuring these items during a period of strict COVID-19 lockdown last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With the easing of travel restrictions, MFA has assisted more Singaporeans overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This figure was twice that of pre-COVID-19 numbers in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MFA also assisted with several complex emergencies, including the evacuation of Singaporeans from conflict areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We worked with our Thai counterparts to facilitate the departure of a Singaporean mother, Olivia, and her baby from Ukraine, where Singapore does not have a diplomatic mission.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Throughout their journey home through Romania, our MFA officers kept in close contact with Olivia to check on their well-being and provide reassurance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This reflects the human and personal touch in MFA's consular assistance, which we endeavour to provide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To help Singaporeans better prepare for their trips, MFA has embarked on new publicity efforts to raise awareness of MFA's consular services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Travel Safe." campaign reminds Singaporeans to e-register, purchase comprehensive travel insurance, and provide tips on how to stay safe while travelling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The safety and well-being of overseas Singaporeans is MFA's priority.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Unfortunately, our officers have occasionally been subjected to abusive behaviour or encountered unreasonable requests, such as receiving Singaporeans at airports, providing security escort services, or interfering in overseas legal or commercial disputes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the heart of MFA's work is a corps of dedicated officers at the frontlines of Singapore's diplomacy every day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms He Ting Ru asked about the challenges faced by and the strengths that women bring to the table in diplomacy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our women serve with courage and distinction at all levels in MFA, including in Senior Management as well as our Ambassadors, bringing to the table a natural collaborative and problem-solving instinct.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: An MFA career is very challenging, for both men and women alike.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The long hours, urgent demands, frequent travel and extended time away from home can take a toll on family life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MFA has in place support systems that help our officers balance the demands of their professional and personal lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For instance, there are provisions that make it conducive for their immediate families to go on post with the officers and support them in maintaining links with their families in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MFA officers have demonstrated resilience and determination amidst all these challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked how we have been engaging Singaporeans on foreign policy and what can be done to counter harmful narratives by foreign actors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Singapore is an open society with a free flow of information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: All countries seek to influence our people and some even interfere outright in our domestic issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is, therefore, critical that Singaporeans understand our national interests and foreign policy objectives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our first and most important line of defence is a vigilant and well-informed citizenry that recognises the geostrategic forces at play and understands our national interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister Vivian, Second Minister Maliki and I, as well as our Ambassadors overseas, our retired Ambassadors and MFA officers have been engaging Singaporeans overseas and in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We do so in schools, though youth organisations and other platforms to communicate Singapore's core interests and the fundamental principles of our foreign policy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will continue to reach out to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman and Members of this House, foreign policy begins at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
text: If we can stay united and work together, we can make Singapore a safe and secure nation in these complex and turbulent times.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I have one clarification on the China-US matter.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: It is clear that Singapore has extensive and deep relations with both countries.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Is there anything that Singapore has envisioned to try and bring both parties together on some of the difficult issues?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We do have good, deep constructive relations with both parties.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We call it the way we see it as a tiny city-state in the heart of Southeast Asia, dependent on world trade.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: They also know that we will be consistently reliable, we are good for our word.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we know our place but we also are useful and credible.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I have a clarification on ASEAN's approach towards Myanmar.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I believe both the Minister and the Second Minister touched on this matter.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: From what I understood, there was an ASEAN decision to exclude Myanmar's junta leaders from ASEAN-level meetings because of disappointment with the implementation of the Five-Point Consensus.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I think that decision was taken in November last year.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But at the same time, we read that a month later in December, Thailand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs apparently hosted a regional meeting, which the junta leaders attended, and which was attended also by Foreign Ministers from Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia and also, I think, from the Vietnam foreign ministry.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And secondly, does he think that the fact that some ASEAN Foreign Ministers attended shows that there is actually a difference of opinion or approach, on how ASEAN should approach Myanmar's junta leaders and the situation in Myanmar in general?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: What is happening in Myanmar is a tragedy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is not something that can be fixed externally.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If you think about Myanmar, since independence – if you go back 70, 80 years, the end of the Second World War – unlike the rest of us, they have never been able to forge a single, all-encompassing consensus on identity and bringing all the component parts together.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is why you, as well as everyone here, will know that Myanmar's people themselves are talented, hardworking, as motivated as anyone else to get ahead and provide for their families.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But unfortunately, the political situation has not enabled Myanmar to create a situation that is conducive for its own people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This coup – two years now in the making – has not helped.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If you ask me for my opinion, I think it is a dead end.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is not going to lead to a road where you will achieve national reconciliation, national reconstruction, the forging of a national identity, the protection of minorities, the uplift of its economy, of its capacity, of its people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Having said that, we must also be very clear that we do not believe in foreign interference in domestic affairs.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, nothing that we do can solve the problem if the key stakeholders within their society themselves are not prepared to sit down and have an honest-to-goodness conversation with each other, for the sake of the future of their people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We must understand that although we clearly disapprove of the coup and we do not recognise the current military junta in Myanmar, it does not give ASEAN a licence to interfere in its domestic affairs.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I hope you agree with me that it is necessary for us to take this principled, but restrained, position on Myanmar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You can argue about why there is this distinction between the political level and the civil service.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The reason for that is because Myanmar remains a member of ASEAN and we do want it to continue to enjoy the benefits of membership to the extent possible within the constraints of its own domestic politics.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We want it to be able to access information which is available to ASEAN.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is why we say, "We are not keeping any secrets from you.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You have a seat at the table." In fact, if you watch the videos of ASEAN leaders' meetings or the foreign ministers' meetings, there is an empty chair.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We do not insist on an empty chair.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We say, "Do not send a political representative because we do not recognise the coup and the military authorities; but by all means, send the most senior civil servant, the Permanent Secretary or the equivalent." Myanmar refuses and would rather keep the chair empty.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I should also say that it does not mean that everyone views the problem in Myanmar through the same prism.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Clearly, the immediate neighbours who face risks of refugee outflows would be in a greater hurry to see a resolution, and perhaps, may be prepared to compromise more on the resolution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For us, we are maintaining a principled position of disapproval.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But whilst the political leaders of Myanmar are not represented at the Summit at the foreign ministers' level, it does not mean that there is no communication, no engagement.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think we need to maintain those lines.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: To give you a short answer, why did I not go for that meeting, which was apparently convened by Thailand?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: First of all, it was not an ASEAN meeting.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It was a bilateral meeting between Thailand and presumably the junta leaders.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I did not think our participation in such a format would be helpful.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I hope you understand why there is a certain amount of restraint but, at the same time, effective engagement is necessary.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is a very difficult and complex problem.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have no idea how long it will take to resolve.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I almost want to say I have to apologise for whatever I have done again.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I know Minister Vivian is very concerned about refugees and has also personally visited the refugee camp.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: As I shared in my cut, it has been six years since we increased our contributions to the UNHCR.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Second, I really do hope we can consider some limited scholarships to a limited number of refugees, so that we can give them some hope and, perhaps, some future in this world we live in.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Like Mr Louis Ng, I have been at the refugee camp at Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh, but even that was some years ago.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The first thing I should say is Bangladesh has, in fact, been extremely generous all these years in hosting and supporting the refugees.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If you had gone to that camp, you would also have noticed that there are multiple agencies, multiple UN agencies and in fact, other countries also, who are providing assistance.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Unfortunately, the real solution is not just assistance at the camp – even though that is urgent and essential.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Because without that, the refugees will not or will choose not to return home, because they worry about their safety for themselves and their family members.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we continue to support and to work through ASEAN.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The answer is, we hope for a definitive solution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But in the meantime, assistance will be needed, humanitarian assistance would be needed, and we will continue to do so, primarily working through ASEAN.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: As the Minister alluded, this is provided for in Article 22 of the ASEAN Charter.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Just now, the Minister mentioned that Myanmar's participation at the political level was reduced.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Was that decision to bar Myanmar's participation at the political level arrived at by consensus or was it a vote?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Or is MFA's position that sticking to the consensus decision-making approach in all cases best serves Singapore's interests?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: The Minister has stated that decision by consensus in ASEAN is a feature, it is not a bug.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: However, does the Minister agree that sometimes features do not work well in all situations?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: No other regional organisation – if you just look at the 10 of us or soon to be 11 – has the great diversity in the economy, forms of government, you have got absolute monarchies, constitutional monarchies, democracies of various shades and, sometimes, even outcomes of coups.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If you look at language, culture, religion – there is no other regional organisation that I can think of with that range of diversity.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, that is the first point – to understand that.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Then, we go back in history – why the consensus principle?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In the midst of diversity, you must remember, it is very important to protect, especially, a community or state or body of opinion that may be a minority at that point in time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: When consensus is abused, it becomes an avenue for everyone to take hostages and to, loosely, threaten a veto.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But actually in practice, knowing that you have to seek consensus creates a whole level of additional consultations, negotiations, compromises, imaginative diplomacy, which would not be present if everyone had easy access to just majoritarian voting.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I explain this at some length, so that you understand why I believe there was good reason for the founders of ASEAN to design the consensus principle.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Whilst I recognise the challenges, it is not something that I am keen to lightly abandon or change.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Coming specifically to Myanmar as a work example.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: When the leaders gathered in April 2021, obviously, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, the State Counsellor of Myanmar and President Win Myint could not attend; they were detained.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The other nine ASEAN leaders were present or sent designated envoys who could act with their authority.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Senior General Min Aung Hlaing, the commander of the Tatmadaw, the Myanmar Armed Forces, attended that meeting.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We did not view his attendance as conferring legitimacy upon him or giving him the status of a Head of State.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Subsequent decisions made, for instance, on the question of political representation, initially made at Foreign Ministers' level and ultimately affirmed at the Leaders' level.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Again, the coup leader was not present at the table.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As far as I am concerned, there was consensus from the ASEAN Leaders, legitimately recognised by each other, the consensus principle continues to operate.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: At the same time, we have been able to express a view that enjoys consensus amongst all the other members of ASEAN.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In life, when you are dealing with complicated situations, be very, very wary about quick fixes and about resorting to simply raising hands.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Sometimes, there are issues for which dialogue, engagement and/or arguments are better conducted, even if it is in a prolonged phase, but with honesty and good faith, I think we can make progress.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In those circumstances, it hands over sufficient flexibility – at least in my opinion – for the leaders to decide how to move forward.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, all in all, as far as this work example is concerned, there will be arguments, but generally, it has worked, and ASEAN has made progress and we have been able to continue negotiations with our external partners, we have been able to sign agreements and the work has gone on.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
